Job Title: Transmission Line Design Engineer or Engineer-in-Training 
 Job Level: ENG B/C/D ( We welcome applications from individuals with all levels of experience and will adjust the title and role accordingly) 
 Date Posted: July 13, 2026
 Closing Date: open until the position is filled
 Job Type: Full-time Permanent
 Category: Internal/External Opportunities 
 Location: Calgary
 Powering a bright future starts with you! 
 Oh, and, what do we do? 
 We power Alberta! Our transmission lines deliver electricity to millions of Albertans 24 hours a day, seven days a week. When you’re on our team, you’re supporting Alberta’s homes, farms, businesses and industries by providing the safe, reliable and affordable electricity they rely on. Whether working in the field or in the office, every AltaLinker contributes to keeping the lights on. Want to join our team? We’re excited to share that we are hiring a Transmission Line Design Engineer.   
 Job Description: 
 An exciting opportunity currently exists for a “Transmission Line Design Engineer” within the Project Development – Lines & Civil Engineering Department at AltaLink. Reporting to the Manager, Lines & Civil Engineering.
 The successful candidate will be responsible for the design, engineering, project development and technical delivery of high voltage transmission line facilities across AltaLink’s transmission line network, from early scoping and conceptual development through detailed design, construction support, close-out and final acceptance. The individual will work closely with internal and external stakeholders to ensure line modifications, line rebuilds, customer interconnections, greenfield transmission line projects and urgent restoration work are designed and supported with a high level of quality, safety, constructability and customer service. 
 The position requires experience in project scoping, design, implementation, technical decision-making, construction support and final acceptance. The role also requires the ability to coordinate multi-stakeholder design inputs, manage design changes, support external EPC and contractor resources, and provide clear technical direction under tight project or field response timelines. As a senior designer on the team, the individual will provide guidance and mentorship to junior engineers and designers. This includes supporting technical development, coaching, design review, and knowledge transfer for emerging engineers and EITs. This position will appeal to individuals looking to apply extensive transmission line design experience and leadership talents in a dynamic utility environment.
 Responsibilities: 
 Prepare detailed calculations, studies, bills of material and design packages for transmission line capital, customer, Direct Assign and system projects.
 Prepare PLS-CADD models for design package development and existing line clearance evaluations.
 Complete line design packages for all AltaLink transmission voltage classes, including 69kV, 138kV, 240kV and 500kV assets, including rebuilds, modifications, greenfield lines, customer interconnections and emergency restoration work.
 Lead preliminary line design, route and structure option development, constructability review, material selection and design change resolution for complex transmission projects.
 Apply base geotechnical knowledge when developing line designs, including understanding soil classifications, borehole/geotechnical investigation outputs, groundwater/bedrock considerations, soil strength/deformation behaviour, frost depth, corrosivity data and backfill requirements as they relate to transmission line foundation selection and constructability.
 Support transmission line foundation design decisions for direct-embed poles, drilled shafts/caissons, screw/helical/bucket piles, driven piles, micro-piles, grillage and pad/footing applications, including review of compression, uplift, shear and moment reactions.
 Coordinate with geotechnical consultants, civil/foundation designers, project managers, construction resources and pile/foundation contractors to define geotechnical scope, review investigation results and resolve foundation design or installation risks.
 Consider foundation risk mitigation during design and construction support, including cave-in/sloughing risk, high groundwater, shallow bedrock, gravel/boulder interference, casing/culvert needs, washed gravel/backfill selection and impacts to schedule, cost, safety and reliability.
 Provide timely and effective technical input to support the Project Development and Execution teams.
 Develop scope descriptions for project estimating and provide clear implementation direction to internal designers, external engineering consultants, EPC contractors, construction resources and field crews.
 Review and/or approve technical drawings and specifications submitted by internal designers or contractors to ensure each project meets acceptable standards for operability, functionality, maintainability, reliability, durability and safety.
 Support construction execution and project close-out by resolving field questions, material issues, redline updates, design clarifications and as-built/return-data requirements.
 Support engineering standards development, design practice improvements and application of current or historical code requirements, including AEUC, CSA and applicable ISO reliability requirements.
 Provide subject matter support for line optimization, line rating, thermal rating, reconductoring assessments, facility applications, information requests and regulatory/hearing support as required.
 Contribute to material governance, supplier engagement, technical specifications, procurement support and emergency spare/material strategy for transmission line assets.
 Build and maintain effective working relationships with suppliers, external technical engineering resources, construction resources, customers and other stakeholders that results in growing understanding, good decisions and effective cooperation.
 Report on project engineering status to Project Managers and the Engineering Manager.
 Mentor junior engineers, EITs and designers through technical coaching, design reviews, knowledge sharing and support toward professional development.
 Provide leadership support within the team as required, including coordination of team deliverables, technical prioritization and coverage for management or project leadership needs.
 Maintain competency with current industry standards and regulatory groups such as AEUC, CSA and ISO Rules.
 Qualifications: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Civil or Electrical Engineering.
 EIT or Professional Engineer with the Association of Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA) or qualifies for registration with APEGA.
 Transmission Line Design experience is considered an asset. 
 Proven ability to perform the responsibilities listed above. 
 Demonstrated experience delivering complex transmission line designs from concept through close-out, including coordination with project managers, external designers, contractors, suppliers and field stakeholders.
 Knowledge of standards and codes that apply to transmission line design and the ability to research and apply past code requirements to existing facilities in current situations, including Alberta power system facilities, Alberta Utility Code (AUC/AEUC) and Canadian Standards Association (CSA) requirements.
 Working knowledge of transmission line materials, structure families, insulator and hardware selection, conductor/OPGW applications, foundations, steel poles, wood poles and constructability considerations.
 Base knowledge of geotechnical investigation programs and geotechnical data used for transmission line design, including borehole/CPT information, soil classifications, soil strength and deformation behaviour, groundwater, bedrock, frost depth, corrosivity and backfill suitability.
 Base knowledge of transmission line foundation design and foundation reaction types, including compression, uplift, shear, overturning moment, lateral soil bearing, embedment depth, pile length/diameter considerations and pole/foundation deflection impacts.
 Ability to interpret geotechnical reports at a level sufficient to coordinate with geotechnical and civil/foundation specialists, identify design or constructability risks, and incorporate appropriate assumptions into line design packages.
 Experience in PLS-CADD and PLS-POLE is required.
 Experience using PLS-Tower, PLS-CAISSON, line rating tools, thermal rating methods, reconductoring assessments or line optimization studies would be an asset.
 Experience supporting customer interconnection, Direct Assign, Facility Application, AESO information request, regulatory/hearing or technical justification work would be an asset.
 Experience developing or applying engineering standards, technical specifications, material procurement requirements or supplier technical evaluations would be an asset.
 Experience with foundation-related standards, geotechnical scope development, foundation constructability reviews, or coordination of engineered foundation designs would be an asset.
 Superior organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage a wide variety of projects/issues simultaneously.
 Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work in a team environment with both office and field staff.
 Demonstrated ability to work under tight timelines and in high stress situations.
 Demonstrated mentoring, coaching or technical leadership experience with junior engineers, EITs, designers or cross-functional project teams.
 Must have a valid class 5 driver’s license.
 Ability and willingness to travel to site as required.
 Effective communication and interpersonal skills to interface with team members and customers to promote positive customer outcomes.
 Proven track record of good performance and attendance.
 Notes: 
 Internal candidates must submit their resume internally via https://referrals.workable.com/altalink/jobs/

 Our occupational therapy team benefits from 1:1 mentorship, including report review and optional drop-in office hours, as well as a comprehensive onboarding program designed for both new graduates and clinicians new to private practice. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in weekly OT team meetings, where we unpack complex cases, share new interventions, and learn from guest speakers.  As an Occupational Therapist at Tall Tree, you’ll play a crucial role in redefining healthcare to prioritize holistic well-being and individualized care. You will deliver high-quality assessment and treatment services to clients facing a range of challenges—from mental health issues and physical injuries to brain injuries and work disabilities. 
 Working collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team and providing services in our clinic, community settings, and through telehealth, you’ll craft personalized therapeutic plans that truly reflect the unique needs of each individual. 
 This is a unique opportunity for a dedicated professional who believes in doing healthcare the way it should be done—by focusing on genuine connections, effective solutions, and the overall health of the individuals we serve. 
 Compensation: 
Full-time (5 days per week) community-based therapists have the opportunity to earn $118,000–$130,000+ annually , along with a signing bonus of up to $5,000 .
 The fee split for this role ranges from 52% to 62% , depending on experience and qualifications.
 As an Occupational Therapist at Tall Tree, you will: 
 Evaluate and assess patients using OT frameworks . You’ll develop individualized treatment plans, and provide exceptional care and interventions that are evidence-based, psychologically informed, and patient-centered.  
 Work collaboratively with our interdisciplinary team of Physiotherapists, Kinesiologists, Psychologists, Clinical Counselors, and more when indicated.  
 Collaborate with third party insurance funders, employers, and other relevant stakeholders . You’ll maintain related reports, records, and statistical data in accordance with established standards and procedures. 
 Keep growing. You’ll attend OT community of practice meetings and other educational opportunities available at Tall Tree. You’ll stay current with the latest evidence, findings, trends, and developments to ensure clients receive the best possible care. 
 We’re looking for: 
 Someone qualified to practice Occupational Therapy in British Columbia. You are a member of the College of Occupational Therapists of British Columbia - with a preference for candidates with 2+ experience in private practice.  
 Comparable experience: You have experience working with third party funders such as WSBC, ICBC and Long Term Disability funders (or provincial equivalents). 
 Clinical Excellence: You have a strong foundation in evidence-based practice and a commitment to mastering skills. You hold a profound respect for the complexity of human experience.  
 Enthusiasm for teaching: You love sharing knowledge and can help mentor colleagues.

We're looking for a Technical Accounting Manager to be our go-to person on technical accounting research, keeping our accounting policies current, and assisting with complex transaction accounting for the company. Position Summary: 
 The Sr. Architect, EWMS Serialization, owns the architecture, design, and ongoing support of serialization capabilities within McKesson’s warehouse management landscape. The role focuses on SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) processes that must capture, verify, and report serialized product data to meet the Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA), and on the integration between SAP EWM, SAP S/4HANA or ECC, and SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals (ATTP). 
 The architect is also accountable for designing, managing, and supporting integrations between SAP and non-SAP systems , including manufacturer and trading-partner platforms, warehouse automation and scanning equipment, carrier and customer systems, and middleware such as SAP Integration Suite (BTP) and SAP Process Orchestration. Operating with high autonomy, the role translates regulatory and operational requirements into reliable, scalable, and audit-ready solutions; serves as the escalation point for complex serialization and integration issues; and partners with business, quality and regulatory, enterprise architecture, vendor, and delivery teams across 3PL and distribution operations. 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Serialization and DSCSA Architecture 
 Own the serialization architecture. Define and maintain the end-to-end target architecture for serialized warehouse processes across SAP EWM, SAP S/4HANA/ECC, and SAP ATTP, aligned to DSCSA requirements and enterprise standards. 
 Design serialized warehouse processes. Lead design of serial number capture, verification, and status updates across inbound receiving, put-away, aggregation and disaggregation (case, pallet, and unit hierarchies), picking, packing, shipping, returns, quarantine, and inventory adjustments. 
 Integrate EWM with ATTP. Architect and support the EWM-to-ATTP and ERP-to-ATTP integration, including material and batch integration, Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) and Serial Shipping Container Code (SSCC) handling, serial number range management, and event posting (commissioning, packing, shipping, receiving, and decommissioning). 
 Enable trading partner data exchange. Design and govern the exchange of serialized transaction data with manufacturers, customers, and partners using EPCIS (Electronic Product Code Information Services) messages, Advance Ship Notices, and related standards. 
 Support DSCSA compliance needs. Translate requirements for package-level tracing, product verification, suspect and illegitimate product handling, saleable returns verification, and data retention into practical system designs and controls. 
 Drive exception handling. Define processes and tooling to identify and resolve serialization data mismatches, missing or duplicate serial numbers, aggregation errors, and failed messages, with clear ownership and audit trails. 
 SAP and Non-SAP Integration 
 Manage the integration landscape. Own the design, documentation, and lifecycle of integrations between SAP (EWM, S/4HANA, ECC, ATTP) and non-SAP systems such as warehouse control systems, scanners and RF devices, label printing, automation equipment, carrier platforms, customer portals, and external serialization or verification networks. 
 Define integration patterns. Select and standardize patterns — APIs, IDocs, web services, events, file transfers, and EDI — using SAP Integration Suite (BTP), SAP Process Orchestration, or other approved middleware, balancing reliability, performance, security, and cost. 
 Ensure reliable operations. Establish monitoring, alerting, error handling, reprocessing, and reconciliation for critical interfaces; lead root-cause analysis for integration and serialization incidents and drive permanent fixes. 
 Onboard partners. Guide technical onboarding of new manufacturers, clients, and trading partners, including mapping, testing, and production readiness for serialized and non-serialized data flows. 
 Delivery, Governance, and Support 
 Lead solution delivery. Lead current-state assessments, fit-gap analysis, solution options, functional and technical specifications, test strategy, cutover planning, and post-go-live stabilization for serialization and integration initiatives. 
 Stay hands-on. Review SAP configuration and custom developments, validate designs and prototypes, and support troubleshooting complex production issues across EWM, ATTP, and interfaces. 
 Govern quality and compliance. Partner with Quality and Regulatory teams to support validation, change control, audit readiness, and documentation in a regulated (GxP) environment. 
 Set standards. Define design principles, reusable patterns, guardrails, and architecture decision records; perform design reviews and manage exceptions. 
 Shape the roadmap. Maintain the serialization and integration roadmap, including SAP S/4HANA and EWM modernization, ATTP upgrades, and cloud integration adoption; evaluate new technologies and recommend improvements. 
 Hold vendors accountable. Guide system integrators and vendors through clear architecture expectations, deliverable reviews, and quality standards. 
 Communicate clearly. Explain designs, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations to executives, business operations, and technical teams in plain language. 
 Mentor and share knowledge. Coach functional and technical team members, lead knowledge-transfer sessions, and maintain runbooks and work instructions. 
 Minimum Job Qualifications: 
 SAP EWM expertise. Deep hands-on knowledge of SAP EWM (embedded and/or decentralized) warehouse processes, including inbound, outbound, internal movements, handling units, packing, RF frameworks, and warehouse monitoring. 
 Serialization expertise. Hands-on experience designing or supporting pharmaceutical serialization integrations with SAP ATTP (or comparable track-and-trace platforms), including serial number management, aggregation hierarchies, GTIN/SSCC handling, and serialization event processing. 
 DSCSA knowledge. Working knowledge of DSCSA requirements and GS1 standards (GTIN, SSCC, EPCIS, barcode data structures) and how they apply to warehouse and distribution operations. 
 SAP ERP integration. Strong understanding of SAP S/4HANA and/or ECC logistics integration (MM, SD, IM, batch management, delivery processing) with EWM and ATTP. 
 Integration skills. Proven experience designing and supporting SAP and non-SAP integrations using IDocs, APIs (REST/SOAP/OData), events, EDI, and middleware such as SAP Integration Suite (BTP), SAP Process Orchestration, or equivalent. 
 Troubleshooting ability. Ability to diagnose cross-system issues across EWM, ERP, ATTP, middleware, and external systems, and turn findings into lasting fixes. 
 Architecture practice. Experience with architecture governance, design reviews, solution roadmaps, and secure-by-design principles; familiarity with frameworks such as TOGAF is a plus. 
 Regulated environment. Experience working under validation, change control, and audit requirements in pharmaceutical, healthcare, or other regulated supply chains. 
 Communication and influence. Strong stakeholder management, facilitation, documentation, and executive communication skills; ability to lead without direct authority. 
 Delivery models. Comfort working in Agile, SAFe, or hybrid delivery models with onshore and offshore teams. 
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Bachelor's degree in information technology, Computer Science, Supply Chain, Engineering, or equivalent combination of education and experience. 
 Typically requires 7+ years of relevant experience in SAP warehouse management, supply chain, or integration architecture, including at least 3 years focused on pharmaceutical serialization and/or SAP ATTP. 
 At least one full-cycle SAP EWM and/or serialization implementation, from design through go-live and stabilization. 
 Demonstrated experience leading medium-to-large, cross-platform initiatives involving SAP and non-SAP systems in complex or regulated environments. 
 Track record of supporting critical production operations, resolving high-impact incidents, and partnering with business, quality, vendor, and delivery teams to deliver measurable outcomes. 
 SAP certification in EWM, ATTP, or SAP Integration Suite.

 Experience integrating warehouse automation, label printing, vision or scanning systems, and external serialization or verification networks. 
 Exposure Lean, Six Sigma, or other process improvement methods. 
 Ability to travel up to 10-20% as needed.

 As a Manufacturing Strategy Specialist, you will work with clients to quickly assess their manufacturing and operational environments, identify improvement opportunities and develop practical recommendations and transformation roadmaps, and then stay with the work through to implementation. This role suits someone who is as comfortable on the plant floor as in the boardroom. You want to see the recommendation running on the line and delivering real results.
 Key responsibilities include:
 Conduct rapid, hands-on assessments of manufacturing facilities and operational environments, spending time on the floor with operators, supervisors and engineers, to identify performance gaps, risks and improvement opportunities.
 Develop broad-based recommendations to improve manufacturing performance, operational efficiency, productivity, cost, quality and sustainability.
 Work with clients to understand their priorities and translate those priorities into actionable manufacturing and operations strategies.

ABOUT JUNIPER SQUARE

Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. We’re the Operations Partner trusted by 2,300+ GPs, unifying technology, data, and fund administration services into a single platform that helps GPs move faster, make better decisions, and scale with precision. With $300B+ under administration and 700,000+ LPs on platform, we’ve built the scale to match our ambition. And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. Founder-led since 2014, backed by $350M+ in funding, and now 1,000+ employees strong, we’re building a company designed to shape the future of private markets for decades to come.

ABOUT YOUR ROLE

Private markets run on trust, and trust travels through networks. GPs compare notes with their peers. LPs validate a manager's credibility before the first meeting happens. The lawyers, auditors, placement agents, and fund administrators who shape a GP’s operations talk to each other constantly.

We're hiring a Head of Editorial and Content to make sure our point of view shapes every one of those conversations, establishing Juniper Square as the reference point for how private markets should operate. In this role, you'll build the brand narrative, editorial authority, and share of voice that make Juniper Square a voice GPs, LPs, and their advisors trust and repeat. Then you'll build the content, web, and social teams that make that authority compound.

This is a builder's role. You'll set the strategy, write and edit when it matters, and hire the people who scale it.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

BRAND NARRATIVE AND POINT OF VIEW

 - Define Juniper Square's market point of view: what we believe about where private markets operations are headed, and why it matters to GPs, LPs, and their advisors.

 - Own the brand narrative and voice across every external channel, and set the editorial standards the rest of GTM writes to.

 - Measure share of voice in private markets conversations and grow it quarter over quarter.

EDITORIAL AND RESEARCH

 - Build a research franchise on Juniper Square platform data leveraging benchmarks and findings the market can't get anywhere else.

 - Create recurring editorial franchises (reports, series, newsletters) that GPs, LPs, and advisors seek out and pass along to peers.

 - Turn what our product, client, and domain experts know into long-form thought leadership, commentary, and analysis.

TRUSTED VOICES AND NETWORKS

 - Map the networks that shape GP decisions across peer GPs, LPs, fund counsel, auditors, placement agents, and fund administrators.

 - Get Juniper Square ideas into those networks, and arm our partnerships and pipeline teams with the research and narrative that open doors.

 - Develop Juniper Square leaders and experts into recognized voices in the market.

SOCIAL AND EXECUTIVE SOCIAL

 - Own Juniper Square's corporate social presence.

 - Run the executive social program, including content strategy and, where needed, ghostwriting for leaders.

CORPORATE WEBSITE AND SEO

 - Own the corporate website's narrative, content, and structure, making it the place private markets leaders go to see how Juniper Square thinks, and come away trusting our perspective

 - Partner with product marketing on the product and asset class pages, so our market point of view and their product messaging tell one connected story.

 - Pick the private markets topics where Juniper Square has to be the authority, then build the SEO and content programs that earn it in both traditional and AI search.

 - Make the site the home for Juniper Square's point of view and research.

TEAM

 - Hire and lead content, web, and social teams.

 - Build the editorial operation behind it all, from planning and intake to review and measurement, so the team publishes on a steady cadence without trading off quality

 - Bring AI tools into the team's workflow to raise quality and scale.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN 12 MONTHS

The conversations that shape where funds land for operations are shaped by our point of view, and Juniper Square is in network with the people having them.

 - GPs, LPs, fund counsel, auditors, placement agents, and fund administrators cite and share Juniper Square ideas in their own networks.

 - A flagship research franchise built on platform data is live, and the market waits for the next edition.

 - Share of voice, branded search, audience, and engagement among target GPs, LPs and partners are measurably up from baseline.

 - Juniper Square leaders have active, credible public voices in private markets.

 - Content, web, and social teams are hired and publishing on a steady cadence.
   
   

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 8+ years in brand, editorial, or content leadership, including building and leading multi-disciplinary teams from early stage.

 - A record of building editorial authority for a B2B brand in a specialized, relationship-driven market, including contributor, community, or expert-voice programs that spread a company's ideas through peer networks.

 - A portfolio of editorial programs you've built, such as research reports, long-form thought leadership, and executive content, with data about their impact, including experience turning proprietary data into published research that a market relies on.

 - Sharp writing and editing, and judgment about what makes an idea travel from one peer to the next.

 - Fluency in measurement, from share of voice and branded search to audience growth, and the ability to report it to an executive team.

 - Experience leading a corporate website and SEO program, and strong partnership with product marketing, revenue marketing, and executives.

 - Practical AI fluency in content workflows. Bring specific examples of AI tools you have configured or connected rather than only used.

 - Nice to have: the curiosity to learn private markets quickly, and experience in financial services, fintech, or private markets.
   
   

COMPENSATION

Compensation for this position includes a base salary, bonus and equity, and a variety of benefits. The U.S. base salary range for this role is $160,000 - $200,000. Actual base salaries will be based on candidate-specific factors, including experience, skillset, and location, and local minimum pay requirements as applicable.

Benefits include:

 - Life insurance

 - Mental wellness coverage

 - Fertility and growing family support

 - Retirement saving plans

 - Annual professional development stipend

James Goodfellow, working at Smiths Industries, uncovered the insight that you needed something you have (a card) and something you know (a PIN). It lets users understand their finances and take action in plain language, from asking about cash flow to sending payments, issuing cards, and managing invoices.  Fondé par le professeur Yoshua Bengio de l’Université de Montréal, Mila rassemble des chercheurs spécialisés en intelligence artificielle et plus précisément en apprentissage automatique, apprentissage profond et apprentissage par renforcement. Reconnu mondialement pour ses importantes contributions au domaine de l’apprentissage profond, Mila s’est particulièrement distingué dans la modélisation du langage, la traduction automatique, la reconnaissance d’objets et les modèles génératifs. Depuis 2017, Mila est le fruit d’une collaboration entre l’Université de Montréal et l’Université McGill, en lien étroit avec Polytechnique Montréal et HEC Montréal.
 À propos du poste 
 Le ou la Conseiller.ère aux projets appliqués offre un soutien opérationnel essentiel à la gestion, à l'avancement et à l'optimisation des équipes de projets appliqués chez Mila. Ce rôle clé assure la coordination transversale de l'équipe ainsi que la mise en œuvre de processus efficaces pour maximiser l'impact des initiatives et la collaboration interne entre les équipes de projets appliquées, mais aussi avec les autres équipes de Mila (e.g., Communications, Partenariats, etc).
 Responsabilités 
 Collaboration, communication et rayonnement 
 Servir d'interface avec les autres équipes ayant des besoins (pitch, description de projets, etc.) pour fournir le matériel ou faciliter la création le cas échéant.
 Assurer un excellent ‘storytelling’ de nos projets en coordination avec l'équipe des communications (métriques de succès, newsletters, blogs, etc.).
 Offrir du support à l'organisation des événements internes et externes.
 Coordonner des démos et des présentations lors de la venue de visiteurs.
 Effectuer la traduction FR-EN et EN-FR au besoin.
 Soutien opérationnel à la croissance de l’équipe 
 Assurer la première ligne de recrutement (descriptions de postes, tri de CVs, etc)
 Coordonner l'accueil et l'intégration (onboarding) des nouveaux employés.
 Supporter les directeurs dans leurs priorités respectives de façons diverses.
 Gestion de l'agenda des meetings statutaires et des activités internes assurant le bon fonctionnement des équipes et des projets.
 Tracking proactif des budgets et des différents projets assignés, surtout lorsqu’il y a plusieurs parties prenantes impliquées.
 Gestion des consultants, des contrats et des ententes avec les autres institutions.
 Implémentation de systèmes et processus permettant à l’équipe de gagner en efficacité.
 Support à la valorisation des actifs 
 Documenter les agents internes que nous construisons, ainsi que leurs fonctionnalités et capacités. 
 Recueillir le feedback des utilisateurs internes, le filtrer et s’assurer qu’il est pris en charge par les bonnes personnes
 Qualités recherchées 
 Autonomie et proactivité : Faire preuve d’une grande initiative pour mener à bien les activités opérationnelles et répondre efficacement aux besoins de l'équipe.
 Rigueur et organisation : Assurer une gestion rigoureuse des projets et des suivis avec un souci constant de la qualité.
 Esprit de collaboration : Travailler efficacement avec des équipes multidisciplinaires et faciliter des interactions harmonieuses et fluides.
 Jugement et esprit analytique : Savoir qui on doit impliquer et quand, pouvoir détecter lorsque du contenu peut sembler sensible. Avoir de bons réflexes en milieu corporatif. 
 Être bilingue , en raison des interactions que vous aurez dans le cadre de votre emploi avec certains de nos partenaires, parties prenantes, ou membres de notre communauté académique anglophones.
 Qualifications 
 Diplôme universitaire dans une discipline pertinente (e.g., administration, gestion, génie, informatique) ou expérience professionnelle équivalente
 5+ ans d'expérience dans un rôle et un environnement similaires
 Maîtrise impeccable du français et de l'anglais, à l'oral et à l'écrit
 Expérience multidisciplinaire (eg. en management consulting ou en start-up) un atout, car ce poste interface avec des fonctions multiples et des gens de tous les niveaux
 De bonnes raisons pour travailler à Mila 
 Un accès à un service de télémédecine;
 Une ambiance de travail collaborative et inclusive.

 Overview

 The Director, Clinical Science – Oncology Clinical Development provides scientific leadership across defined components of study design, conduct, data review, and interpretation within an assigned clinical programme. Reporting to the Clinical Development Lead (CDL), this role operates within the asset-level clinical strategy and contributes scientific depth and rigour to the execution of the Clinical Development Plan (CDP).
 The Director, Clinical Scientist partners closely with the Senior Scientist and cross-functional teams to support delivery of clinical studies, ensuring scientific quality, data integrity, and robust interpretation of clinical data. This role contributes to both study-level activities and broader programme insights, without holding accountability for asset-level strategy or overall study delivery.
 This is a scientific individual contributor role requiring deep oncology clinical development expertise, strong analytical and collaboration skills, and the ability to operate effectively within a complex, matrixed environment.
 In This Role You Will:
 Provide scientific leadership across defined components of study-level activities, including protocol development, study design, data review, and interpretation, within the strategic direction set by the CDL
 Serve as a core member of the Clinical Matrix Team (CMT), ensuring scientific alignment across study objectives, timelines, and deliverables
 Provide scientific insight to the CDL and Senior Scientist to inform asset-level strategy, benefit–risk assessment, and programme-level decision-making
 Ensure the scientific quality and consistency of key clinical and regulatory documents, including protocols, Investigator’s Brochures, Clinical Study Reports, and submission materials
 Apply scientific and clinical expertise to analyse and interpret data, ensuring rigour, integrity, and relevance to the target patient population
 Engage with internal and external stakeholders, including investigators and Key External Experts, to support study execution and scientific exchange
 Contribute to a culture of scientific excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement within Oncology Clinical Development
 Detailed Responsibilities: 
 Study Design and Execution
 Provide scientific input into protocol development and study design, ensuring robustness, feasibility, and alignment with CDP-defined objectives and regulatory requirements
 Author or co-author key study documents (e.g., Clinical Study Proposals), contributing to preparation and presentation at governance forums such as Protocol Review Boards
 Support study conduct by addressing scientific questions, ensuring data integrity, and maintaining alignment with protocol and regulatory standards
 Provide scientific input into study-level decisions related to protocol implementation and study conduct, within the strategic framework defined by the CDL
 Present and support the scientific rationale and study design at Investigator Meetings and respond to scientific inquiries from study sites
 Support implementation of study-level Go/No-Go criteria aligned to the asset-level decision framework defined by the CDL
 Data Generation, Analysis, and Interpretation
 Analyse and interpret clinical data to generate insights on safety, efficacy, and patient populations
 Integrate data from internal and external sources (e.g., literature, competitor data, emerging science) to inform study and programme understanding
 Provide scientific input into data review and interpretation activities, in collaboration with Medical Directors and pharmacovigilance
 Translate study findings into clear scientific insights to inform programme progression and support CDL-led decision-making
 Clinical and Regulatory Deliverables
 Contribute to development of clinical and regulatory documents, including protocols, Investigator’s Brochures (IBs), Clinical Study Reports (CSRs), and submission materials
 Ensure scientific accuracy, consistency, and quality across study documentation
 Support preparation of regulatory submissions and responses to Health Authority queries
 Contribute to regulatory reporting requirements (e.g., DSURs, INDSRs) and ensure alignment with regulatory standards
 Cross-Functional Collaboration & Scientific Contribution
 Serve as a core member of the CMT, partnering with Clinical Operations, Statistics, Safety, Regulatory, and Medical Affairs to support integrated study delivery
 Provide scientific expertise to cross-functional discussions, including integrated evidence planning and disease-area forums, as appropriate
 Participate in internal and external scientific interactions with investigators, Key External Experts, advisory boards, and collaborators
 Contribute to scientific communications, including publications, congress presentations, and study-related materials
  Ways of Working & Continuous Improvement
 Identify scientific and operational risks at the study level and provide input into mitigation strategies
 Support and drive implementation of consistent ways of working and process improvements across the programme
 Participate in Oncology Clinical Development initiatives and workstreams to strengthen standards, processes, and capabilities
 Engage in ongoing development to deepen scientific expertise, expand disease-area knowledge, and build broader clinical development capabilities
 Why You? 
 Working model: 
 This role is hybrid. You will be on-site at one of the posted locations at least two days per week. Remote work is available on other days.
 Basic Qualifications 
 We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals: 
 ·      Bachelor’s degree in life sciences or related scientific discipline required
 ·      5+ years of experience in pharmaceutical/biotechnology industry or related clinical development experience, with a focus on oncology.
 ·      Experience in clinical development from early stage through to regulatory submission, including study design, protocol authoring, and data review/interpretation.
 ·      Experience working within GCP, ICH, and global regulatory guidelines.
 ·      Experience authoring or contributing to clinical study proposals, protocols, Investigator’s Brochures, informed consent forms, clinical study reports, and regulatory submissions.
 ·      Experience working within cross-functional matrix teams and contributing to clinical decision-making.
 ·      Proven track record of working with investigators, site staff, external experts, CROs, and vendors.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 ·      Advanced degree (e.g. MS, PhD, PharmD) strongly preferred in life sciences or a related discipline
 ·      Clinical development experience across multiple phases of development (Phase I–IV)
 ·      Oncology or immuno-oncology clinical development experience.
 ·      Experience presenting or preparing materials for Protocol Review Boards, governance meetings, or scientific forums. 
 ·      Knowledge of regulatory requirements to support registration, including experience contributing to IND, EoP2, scientific advice, pre-NDA/BLA, NDA/MAA, or AdCom submissions.
 What we value 
We act with transparency, respect and integrity. We welcome different perspectives and champion inclusion. Bring curiosity, humility and a clear focus on patients.
 Ready to apply? 
If you want to help shape clinical development and make a real difference for patients, we would like to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a short cover letter describing your relevant experience and why this role matters to you. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to inclusion.

Analytical Thinking, Business Acumen, Change Management, Clinical Research, Clinical Trial Designs, Communication, Decision Making, Fostering Collaboration, Influencing Without Authority, Leadership, Matrix Leadership, Mentorship, People Management, Risk Management, Strategic Thinking

WHY HARVEY

FUNCTION OVERVIEW

Harvey's Legal Engineering team is composed of former practicing attorneys who work to bring value to Harvey's prospects and customers. Legal Engineers lead discovery, demos, trainings, and onboarding alongside our AEs and CSMs. They translate real legal work into Harvey solutions, serving as the trust layer across the entire customer lifecycle, from the first pilot to the most complex, custom-built workflow.

At Harvey, we segment the Legal Engineering function into three teams: Legal Engineers (Pre-Sales), Legal Engineers, Product Specialists (Post-Sales), and Legal Engineers, Custom Solutions (Pre- and Post-Sales). Legal Engineers across all three subgroups understand how lawyers think and work, and use that expertise to design, build, and refine solutions that hold up under live in-practice pressure. In doing so, they don't just drive adoption; they shape Harvey's product roadmap, ensuring every release is grounded in what the legal profession needs. It's a team built to power Harvey as the platform lawyers can trust with their most important work.

 

You may be asked to travel around 2-3+ times per month. Travel is always for a significant business need and typically is for 1-3 days at a time.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Legal Engineer (Pre-Sales)

Legal Engineers are lawyers who left practice to help build the future of legal work. Working closely with Account Executives, they engage with many of the world’s leading law firms and legal teams throughout the pre-sales process. They lead collaborative pilot programs, guide prospects through what’s possible with AI, and work alongside lawyers to understand their workflows, build tailored solutions, and demonstrate meaningful value in real legal use cases. Along the way, they bring prospect feedback back into the product, helping shape the future of Harvey.

 

Legal Engineer, Product Specialist (Post-Sales)

LEPS take over once a prospect becomes a customer. LEPS build trusted relationships with many of the world's leading legal teams by learning their workflows and showing them how to weave Harvey into daily practice.  The LEPS role spans the entire customer journey, from leading onboarding and enablement, to sitting down with a full practice group to build agents on real matters. Along the way, the LEPS translates legal practice needs into actionable feedback for product and engineering, contributes to customer-facing content across practice areas, and upholds Harvey's credibility as the leading AI platform for lawyers.

 

Legal Engineer, Custom Solutions (Pre-Sale and Post-Sale)

LECS are a specialist group that work on complex no-code custom Harvey in-app solutions. LECS meet with group heads, general counsel, and other senior stakeholders to learn how key processes run today. Drawing on their legal expertise, they use natural language prompting to design bespoke resources, including agents, playbooks, and other tools, that improve the quality, speed, and experience of that process. The build is collaborative. The LECS scope it with the customer, prototype against sample documents, and refine it alongside their team. Most LECS work happens post-sale, but the team also supports strategic accounts pre-sale on an advisory basis. LECS concentrates narrowly on designing tools that automate a specific process, and on building relationships with the senior leaders who own it.

 

*In your initial interview with our recruiting team, you'll learn more about all three roles, and we'll identify which may be the best fit based on your background and our current hiring needs.

What You Have

You move confidently through uncertainty, you operate at speed, and ship solutions that work—iterating quickly with lawyers, sales teams, and product partners to help Harvey and its customers win. You bring deep curiosity about AI's potential to transform legal work, a bias toward action, and the creativity to solve problems nobody's cracked yet.

 - Based in Toronto and eligible to work in Canada.

 - Canadian practicing certificate (or equivalent common-law qualification) with 3+ years’ experience as a qualified lawyer, including meaningful in-house experience at a corporation or financial institution (with prior top-tier law firm experience strongly preferred).

 - Strong background as a corporate attorney, with hands-on experience advising on corporate, commercial, and/or regulatory matters within an in-house legal team.

 - Deep understanding of corporate legal workflows (e.g., commercial contracting, governance, compliance, or transactions) and curiosity about how AI can reshape them.

 - Proven ability to navigate business-oriented legal environments, balancing legal risk with practical commercial outcomes.

 - Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment and make confident, well-reasoned recommendations in fast-paced, ambiguous settings.

 - Ability to operate seamlessly across legal, product, and sales contexts—translating between stakeholders with clarity and precision.

 - Executive presence and strong relationship-building skills, with experience engaging business stakeholders, senior leadership, and cross-functional partners.

 - Experience working cross-functionally with product, sales, or business teams in an in-house setting; customer-facing or business development experience is a plus.

 - French speaking is a plus. 

COMPENSATION

CAD $192,800 - $289,200 OTE 75/25
